correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, only same-part pairs are nonadjacent, and every geodesic between two such vertices has exactly one internal vertex outside their part. This reduces dual visibility to the stated complement-outside-part condition. The invalid-set families then have the two stated forms according to whether a part has order two or at least three, and their pairwise intersections consist only of the full vertex set, giving the polynomial by inclusion-exclusion. The two-color constructions cover every finite branch, while the center of \(K_{1,n}\) with \(n\ge3\) lies in no dual set. A generic shortest-path checker exhaustively agrees through order eight.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete all-set profile, an exact generating polynomial, and the chromatic classification for a canonical graph class in a parameter introduced in 2026. The \(n_i=2\) exception in the polynomial and the sharp \(K_{1,2}\) versus \(K_{1,n}\), \(n\ge3\), transition are structural features not visible from maximum-set values alone. This is a natural classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
